sites.functional_impact_measured: NOT MEASURED — the ledger clip describes construct design and subcloning for heterologous expression; no specific assay result (surface staining, cAMP, calcium imaging) is reported in the clip.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly reports a full-length, membrane-anchored OR2C1 construct carrying an N-terminal Rho tag, satisfying the requirement for a tolerated insertion in a membrane-anchored protein. Topology landmarks place residues 1–24 as extracellular with no signal peptide, so the tag prepends before M1 (insert_after_residue=0); this is the sole extracellular terminus and the position is topology-derived, not chosen. Python confirms seq[0]='M' (residue_after) and the TM1 boundary begins at residue 25, placing the prepend 24 residues from the nearest TM helix, well above the ≥3-residue minimum. No specific residue number is cited in the clip, so position_evidence is topology_derived and evidence_type cannot be the exact-site value. Full-length OR2C1 was engineered with an N-terminal rhodopsin (Rho) tag and subcloned into a pCI expression vector for heterologous expression (PMC9861704). The paper states 'N-terminal' but names no specific residue number. OR2C1 has no signal peptide (topology confirms residues 1–24 are extracellular, no 'S' state), so the N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus available for a prepend, making insert_after_residue=0 the unique solution.

sources.claim: The full-length genomic of OR2C1 was amplified by the specific primers tag with N-terminal rhodopsin and was subcloned into pCI vector between Mlu I and Not I restriction enzyme sites.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is provided. It supports a single N-terminal Rho-tag site on full-length OR2C1 expressed heterologously. The three extracellular loops (ECL1: 80–99, ECL2: 167–196, ECL3: 257–272) and the C-terminal intracellular tail have no ledger support and are therefore not proposed as sites. The Rho tag used here is the standard N-terminal rhodopsin sequence (typically the first ~9–20 aa of bovine rhodopsin, e.g. MNGTEGPNFY…) routinely prepended to olfactory receptors to improve surface trafficking and enable immunodetection; its placement at the extracellular N-terminus of a GPCR lacking a signal peptide is unambiguous. Validation level is not_measured because the clip describes only construct construction and subcloning, not a surface-expression or functional assay result.
